newsitem.title: USA: Littelfuse sees '97 growth below Q4 level.
newsitem.headline: Littelfuse sees '97 growth below Q4 level.

text.p: Littelfuse Inc said it expects growth in 1997 will continue, although not as briskly as it did in the fourth quarter ended December 28.

"Looking ahead, Littelfuse expects 1997 to bring continued improvement in its performance," the company said. "However, the growth is not expected to be quite as strong as it was in the fourth quarter of 1996," said chief executive Howard Witt.

The maker of electronic, power and automotive fuses said Wednesday that sales for the fourth quarter reached $61 million, up 16 percent over the year-ago period. Quarterly net income grew by 31 percent to $5.5 million.

Earnings per share increased by 35 percent to $0.46, compared with $0.34 in the fourth quarter of 1995, in part because of company's stock/warrant repurchase program reduced the number of shares outstanding, it said.

"Our results matched our expectations," Witt said. "Although 1996 got off to a relatively slow start, the strong growth we achieved in the third and fourth quarters brought double-digit gains for the year."
For the year ended December 28, sales grew 10 percent over 1995 to $241.4 million.
"Our results reflect the gradual improvement of our worldwide markets during the year," said Witt.
